first.rationale: The two measured declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the same upstream funnel stage, and onboarding completion feeding activation is the most plausible causal chain. memory_86 and memory_31 both support onboarding/signup simplification, and it is the only candidate that targets the observed regression rather than compensating for it elsewhere. I am verifying memory_86 because it is the direct basis for my intended action and consolidated summaries lose the conditions under which the lift held (which segments, whether the lift persisted past week one, whether 'completion' was measured as a proxy or as real time-to-value). I am verifying memory_73 because promotional pricing is the obvious reflexive answer to the competitor's entry pricing and carries the largest downstream value risk: 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' in a consolidated note is exactly the phrasing that can survive summarization while the retention, discount-cohort LTV, and margin effects are dropped. Under a mandate for sustainable long-term qualified revenue, I want the original record before ruling it in or out rather than trusting the compressed claim. Caveats I am carrying forward: memory_31 achieved its lift by cutting required signup fields, which can degrade lead qualification and routing and thus trade activation volume for qualified revenue, so the test needs downstream quality guardrails (lead-to-opportunity rate, 30/60-day retention, ARPA of the treated cohort), not just completion and activation. memory_44 also implies enterprise pipeline depends on the sales-assisted path, so any simplification should be scoped to self-serve/SMB and not strip fields used for enterprise routing. All six memories are consolidated day-12-to-61 summaries with archived sources; the environment has since changed (new competitor, declining metrics), so their effect sizes should be treated as directional priors, not as predictions. If the memory_73 record shows durable qualified revenue rather than discount-driven churn, I will reconsider; standard experiment scale with a holdout, not a broad rollout.
